48. People on a low income, or whose social network does not include professionals, are less
likely than those in a more privileged position to gain access to timely legal advice and
representation. This is an increasingly pressing issue for the justice system in the light of
former legal aid reforms.

49. People may come to a court or tribunal not really knowing why they are there, or what the
potential outcomes are. Even where it is their own case, they may have only a hazy
understanding of what it is about, particularly if they have been advised by an organisation at
